{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging", "description": "Knowing the parent went to bat publicly puts the kid in an awkward spot with teammates — they may feel marked as the player who needed a parent to argue their case." },
  "read": "The kid is caught in the worst of both worlds: they may privately agree with the parent, but having it aired to the coach strips them of any agency in the matter and signals to everyone watching that they can't handle their own standing on this team. Their status feels like it's being assigned by a parent instead of earned, which is humiliating even when the underlying desire is legitimate.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Double down on the depth chart to prove the decision belongs to you, maybe with a cold shoulder toward the player — backfires because it punishes the kid for something the parent did and hardens the relationship at exactly the wrong moment." },
  "mentorMove": "Separate the parent conversation from the player conversation entirely. Let the kid know you see them as someone capable of having this conversation themselves, then open a direct, honest dialogue about what earning more reps actually looks like — keeping the standard firm while giving them a real path.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "Playing time decisions are yours and stay grounded in what you see in practice and games — that standard does not move because of an email.",
    "The player still has to earn it the same way everyone else does, and you name that clearly."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "You can share exactly what you are looking at when you make lineup decisions, so the player has real, actionable information instead of a wall.",
    "You can invite them to check in with you more often, set short benchmarks, even ask them what they think they need to work on — widen the how without softening the what."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, can you hang back two minutes after we wrap up? Just want to check in with you — nothing bad, I just want to talk to you directly." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "I know your folks sent me a note, and I figure you probably know that too. Before I say anything else — how are you actually feeling about where things stand right now? I want to hear it from you, not from an email." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Okay. Here is exactly what I am watching for when I set the lineup — and I mean the specific stuff, not just general effort. I want you to know what the real target is, because you deserve that clarity. And honestly, I'd rather you come knock on my door when you're frustrated than have it go through anyone else — that's between us." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I have high standards for this role, and I'm telling you straight: I think you have the ability to get there. That's not a line — it's why I'm having this conversation with you instead of just moving on. So let's figure out together what the next two weeks look like for you, and then let's see what you do with it." }
  ],
  "longGame": "The goal is to make this player feel like a full participant in their own development rather than a case being managed between adults. If they start bringing their frustrations to you instead of their parents, you have built something real — and that trust will matter far more than any single spot in the lineup."
}
situation: A player's parent emailed me arguing their kid should be starting, and the kid clearly knows about the email.
